newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentina's Disco to buy supermarkets for $72 mln.
newsitem.headline: Argentina's Disco to buy supermarkets for $72 mln.

text.p: Argentina's supermarket chain Disco Tuesday announced it has agreed to acquire 100 percent of the outstanding shares of local supermarket chain Su Supermercado for $72 million.
The closing of the transaction is expected to occur in July, Disco said in a statement.
Disco, controlled by Argentina's Grupo Velox, said Su Supermercado posted sales of $248 million in fiscal year ended August 31, 1996.
Su Supermercado currently operates one supermarket in Buenos Aires and 14 in Greater Buenos Aires.
Disco said the acquisition will strenghten its presence in the Greater Buenos Aires Area, where Disco currently operates 10 stores.
"This step further reinforces our strategy of consolidating our positioning within the Argentine food retail industry," said Eduardo Orteu, Disco's Chief Executive Officer.

"We believe the stores incorporated through this acquisition...will perfectly complement our current business, allowing us to further penetrate Greater Buenos Aires, without sacrificing the sales of our existing stores."
Chile's supermarket chain Santa Isabel said in May its President of the Board, Eduardo Elberg, was planning to sell to Disco his 36.96 percent stake for $230 million.
